Best Places to Buy Affordable School Supplies in DFW

July 31, 2026 by Chelsea White
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 5:00
Instaread

The summer has flown by, and it’s already time to stock up on school supplies for the school year. But as everything gets more and more expensive, that school supply list can start looking like a money pit. Luckily, if you’re looking for the best places to buy affordable school supplies in DFW, there are a lot of options, including big box stores, grocery stores and even some secondhand stores. And don’t forget to check for weekly sales.

Combination of stores

If you’re serious about getting the best prices on the supplies you need (and don’t mind doing a little homework), the best solution is to check out several of the following stores’ prices on specific items. While Walmart is the best overall, there are often some items that have better prices at other stores. If you’ve got the time and determination, shop around.

Walmart 

We all know Walmart has everything, and that includes low prices. So it’s no wonder that Walmart is consistently the most affordable place to buy school supplies in DFW. If you’re looking for a one-stop shop (or even delivery so it all just shows up on your doorstep), Walmart is most likely to have the best prices overall. 

You can search for your specific school’s and grades’ supply lists, and Walmart will show you all the products so you can add them to your cart all at once (Target also has this option). 

In terms of prices, when comparing a school’s list at Walmart vs. Target using this feature (a Fort Worth ISD first grade supply list), the total price at Walmart was about $50 while the price at Target was about $91. 

And while some of the more specialty items (like pipe cleaners and ear buds) raised the Target price, this is still a good example of how Walmart is the easiest spot for finding affordable options without much hassle.

Target

If you love a good Target run (and who doesn’t love a good Target run?), it’s a great spot for checking off your school supply list. While Walmart may have beat Target overall for low school supply prices, when looking at individual items, Target is often comparable and sometimes the most affordable. 

Target’s Up and Up generic brand is a great affordable alternative to some of the more expensive brand names. Plus they have great sales (especially if you’re a Target Circle member).

Dollar Tree

Don’t forget about dollar stores when you’re on the hunt for the most affordable school supplies. Local moms often suggest Dollar Tree as one of the best spots to check off your list. Most items are $1.25 each, so you know exactly what prices to expect. 

Creative Reuse Stores

There are lots of supplies you’ll need or want to buy brand new for your list, but if you’re looking at getting some extra supplies or you’re a teacher stocking up for the year, reuse stores are a treasure trove of options. There are lots of arts and crafts supplies, but also office and school supplies to fill your shelves and pencil boxes. The challenge and the beauty of these stores is that you never know exactly what you’re going to find. Typical offerings may include binders, notebooks, hole punchers, watercolors, markers, rulers, scissors, and more.

Check out one of these secondhand centers:

  • Untrash Creative Reuse in Richardson
  • Pegasus Creative Reuse in Dallas 
  • Thistle Creative Reuse in Denton

If you’re a teacher shopping for your classroom (or on a PTA/PTO shopping for your school), you’ve also got to check out The Welman Project in Fort Worth. Get as many free supplies as you want or need from the Educator Warehouse. You can find secondhand and donated items like office supplies, classroom decor, books, party supplies, storage solutions, and more.

Grocery Stores

Don’t forget the stores you shop weekly! Your local grocery store may or may not have every item on your school supply list depending on its size, but you might find some of the best deals there. And you can just add it on to your weekly visit!

Looking at H-E-B, for example, there are several common school supplies that are price-matched to Walmart’s prices, as well as great prices on store-brand supplies. 

Check out your preferred store to see if the prices are worthwhile.

Tax-Free Weekend

Tax-free weekend in Texas for 2026 is August 7-9 — maybe too late to get the bulk of your school supplies since many districts go back for the new year just a few days later. But if you don’t mind waiting or you just need a few last things, a tax-free weekend is a good chance to save a little bit on school supplies, back-to-school clothes and shoes, backpacks and more. Without sales tax, you save $8.25 on every $100 of qualifying purchases.

Here’s wishing you and your families a happy school year (full of the perfect school supplies that didn’t break the bank)!

Any other suggestions for the best places to buy affordable school supplies in DFW? Let us know in the comments!
